title: Mira’s Bridge
brief: Hoo! Let’s step off the Reading Road. In “The Choice at the Bridge,” Mira walks onto a narrow bridge to help a boy. Find a crossing like hers, then take a photo for your teacher.
look: This stop is a narrow bridge like Mira’s. Text 1 says courage means you act even when you are afraid. This time you don’t build. You find a place.

lookfors.name: A narrow crossing
lookfors.why: a bridge, a narrow street or a thin path

lookfors.name: Two sides
lookfors.why: Mira on one side, the boys on the other

steps.title: Know what to look for
steps.text: You won’t build today. You will find a crossing like Mira’s. Read the three things to look for. This list is also in VR, in the **Canvas** tab.

steps.title: Find it
steps.text: Walk and teleport through the town. Find a narrow place to cross, with one side and another side. No bridge? A narrow street works.

steps.title: Look closely
steps.text: Stand at your crossing and say this out loud:
steps.spoken: Stand at your crossing and say this out loud. Mira was brave because… Courage means…

extra.text: Take one step forward, like Mira. Say one brave thing a kid your age could do.

points: Your photo shows a narrow crossing with two sides.

mapday.intro: No headset today? It’s Road Map Day. Read each line and tap which text it comes from. Then finish two sentences about courage.
mapday.miss: Not that one. Is it a fact about courage, or part of Mira’s story?
mapday.done: ✓ You sorted every line. Now finish the two sentences.

names.t2: Text 2, The Choice at the Bridge

scene.aria: A town with a spot for Text 1 and a spot for Text 2

clues.q: “Courage is not the same as having no fear.”
“In fact, most courageous acts involve fear.”
Plato named courage as one of the four most important virtues.
“I just decided that he mattered more than my fear did.”

frames.start: Mira chose to act anyway because
hints: the boy mattered more than her fear
